summary: This bill replaces the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases by renaming it the National Institute of Allergic Diseases (limited to allergic conditions), creating a new National Institute of Infectious Diseases, and creating a new National Institute of Immunologic Diseases, with corresponding transfers of authorities, new presidentially appointed directors serving 5-year terms, and conforming amendments to the Public Health Service Act.

scores.thoughts: The bill reorganizes the structure of NIH institutes by splitting one into three but makes no changes to funding levels, appropriations, or overall government expenditures. It is a purely administrative restructuring with no bearing on spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue policy.

While the bill affects NIH research institutes involved in health-related research, it is strictly a structural reorganization and does not address healthcare coverage, access, public vs. private systems, or market-based reforms.
